MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS FOR THE PERIOD ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026
NEWS RELEASE DATED NOVEMBER 8, 2026 - THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS AND OPERATIONAL
NEWS RELEASE DATED NOVEMBER 8, 2026 - STRATHCONA RESOURCES LTD. ANNOUNCES AGREEM

desk.headline: Output up 72% after Connacher deal, oil sales up 116% to C$305m; net loss C$21m on hedging losses; Strathcona agrees to buy Greenfire

other.label: Loss on hedging contracts
other.change: vs C$9.8m loss a year ago

other.label: Net debt
other.change: vs net cash of C$49.7m at end-2025

results: Bitumen output rose 72% to 27,166 bbl/d, mainly from the Great Divide asset bought with Connacher on 5 Aug 2026 for C$1.30bn in cash.
Oil sales more than doubled to C$305.3m on higher volumes and a 34% rise in Canadian-dollar heavy-oil prices, but royalties jumped to 19% of sales from 5.5%.
Hedges cost C$54.7m (C$36.9m realised), turning the quarter into a net loss of C$21.0m, or C$0.15 a share, from C$8.8m a year ago.
Adjusted EBITDA rose to C$62.8m and adjusted funds flow to C$49.2m; capex was C$40.6m.
The deal was funded by a C$774.3m rights offering and a C$1.0bn credit facility; net debt was C$587.1m at quarter-end, with C$430m undrawn.

guidance.summary: The filed statements and MD&A give no numeric production, cash-flow or capex guidance. They set project timelines: full Expansion plant capacity of about 26,000 bbl/d by 2028, with Pad 5SE first oil brought forward to Q1 2027.

watch: Progress of the Strathcona takeover, announced alongside the results, which Waterous Energy Fund (72% owner) supports.
Ramp-up of Pad 7 (first oil in November 2026) and first steam at Pads 5SE and 8.
Hedging losses and royalty costs while oil prices stay high.

sources.title: Strathcona to acquire Greenfire in $2.1-billion oil sands deal — World Oil, 9 Nov 2026
